newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dow boosts Eurobourses ahead of U.S. poll.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dow boosts Eurobourses ahead of U.S. poll.

text.p: A bullish opening on Wall Street ahead of U.S. presidential election results and the apparently successful conclusion of Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery boosted European bourses on Tuesday.
On the currency markets the dollar held slim gains against the mark but, generally speaking, both equity and currency trading was thin, analysts said.
In Moscow doctors involved in Yeltsin's bypass operation declared it a complete success and said he would be able to resume normal work.

Russian debt and equity traded overseas reacted positively to the news. In London, Europe biggest bourse, leading shares had already recouped most of their morning losses before New York trading begun but Wall Street's firm opening gave a further boost.
The blue chip FTSE 100 index, which had earlier fallen to its lowest level in six weeks, was down 2.5 at 3925.6 shortly after Wall Street opened, well up from its intraday low of 3,911.0 points.
At 1500 GMT the Dow was up 30 points or half a percentage point at 6072.
Dealers said the British market's weakness was surprising, given Wall Street's strength overnight and the respectable performances from bourses across Europe.

"It seems we are more worried about the U.S. elections than the U.S., the French and Germans combined...There were a lot of worries about the Democrats getting Congress as well as the White House but people now seem to think that's unlikely so this drop is perhaps overdone," one dealer said.
Among factors holding London back was Britain's biggest clothing retailer, Marks & Spencer, whose shares dived as results came in below expectations.
Early morning news that Yeltsin's operation had begun boosted the dollar marginally against the mark as the German currency is traditionally vulnerable to any uncertainty in Russia.

The dollar was holding its gains on the mark in afternoon. A sharp 3.6 percent fall in German industry orders for September, coming hard on the heels of Monday's unexpected 1.8 percent drop in September industrial output, did not help mark sentiment.

"German manufacturing orders came out much softer than expected and will tend to keep a cap on the upside for the mark and expectations about the German economy," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economic adviser at Bank of America in London. The markets were counting on re-election for President Bill Clinton and maintained Republican control of Congress, dealers said. But, they warned, a Democrat "clean sweep" could upset the dollar.
At 1500 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 1.5138 marks, down from late Monday's European level of 1.5142 but well off an overnight low of 1.5075.

The Swiss franc was boosted in early trade by nerves surrounding Yeltsin's heart surgery, but had pulled back by European mid-session after Moscow hospital sources said the operation had been completed successfully.
And Sterling continued its sparkling bull run, hitting $1.6560 -- its best level since March 1995 -- and sizing up key chart resistance around $1.6575.

In Frankfurt stocks ended bourse trade at the day's high and forged ahead further in post-bourse electronic trading after the Wall Street's firm start. German shares were boosted by government bonds which had risen on reports that Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation had been successfully completed.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares closed floor trade up 19.43 points, or 0.73 percent, at 2,691.29.

In Paris French shares soared in the afternoon -- up 1.5 percent -- in modest turnover on the back of new highs in the bond markets and news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had come through seven hours of open heart surgery.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT The dollar was trading at 1.5138 marks and 113.72 yen compared with late Monday's 1.5142 marks and 113.93 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 2.5 points lower at 3,925.6.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 31.54 at 2,173.69
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 19.43 at 2,691,29.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $379.25 compared with $379.05 at the London close on Monday. Silver was at $4.83.
